newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds creep higher, outperform Bunds.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds creep higher, outperform Bunds.

text.p: Irish government bonds crept higher in thin trade on Monday, outperforming German Bunds in the five and 10-year areas of the curve thanks to mild foreign buying, dealers said.
"It has been a very thin day for volumes but there was a bit of foreign buying in the five-year and the 10-year areas," one dealer said. "Spreads with Germany have narrowed slightly as a result."
By 1500 GMT the eight percent bond due 2000 was up 10p at 106.70 while the eight percent bond due 2006 was 15p higher at 107.55.
Dealers said the Irish pound's weakness against sterling would remain a focus for the market. At 1507 GMT the punt was hovering not far above parity with sterling at 1.0070.

"The Irish market has not enjoyed this bout of punt weakness versus sterling over the last couple of weeks, and would get very nervous if the punt were allowed to fall below par, despite towering punt strength in the ERM," Riada Stockbrokers said in a daily note.
But NCB Stockbrokers said fears of the inflationary effects of a lower punt/sterling rate were "overly panicky".
It said the idea that UK inflation and the punt/sterling exchange rate were the main determinants of Irish inflation was not borne out by experience.
"Even were the UK inflation/sterling dominance theory correct, we are only unwinding part of the beneficial impact of earlier appreciation in the Irish pound," NCB said.
